title: Horseshoe crabs aren't crabs: they're closer kin to spiders and scorpions

cover.alt: An upside-down horseshoe crab lies in the shallow surf, its legs sticking up out of its dark, bowl-shaped shell.

body: Despite the name and the hard shell, horseshoe crabs are not crustaceans: they are more closely related to arachnids such as spiders and scorpions. Their lineage is ancient, with fossils from rocks **445 million years old**, and they have changed little since. Waves and currents often flip them over, which can leave them stranded and suffocating, and the long spike of a tail, the telson, may help them lever themselves upright again.

slides.alt: In the surf, an upside-down horseshoe crab rocks onto its edge and balances there as waves wash past; then a wave tips it, its spiky tail flicks up, and it lands the right way up and moves off.
slides.caption: On Plumb Beach in New York, an upside-down horseshoe crab rocks onto its edge as waves wash over it, until one wave tips it back onto its legs.
slides.music: “Goblin Tinker Soldier Spy” Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com) · CC BY 4.0

slides.heading: Which of these is not a crustacean?
slides.explanation: Lobsters, shrimp and crabs are crustaceans. Scorpions are arachnids, like spiders, and arachnids are the horseshoe crab's closer kin.

slides.label: years old: the oldest horseshoe crab fossils, from Manitoba, Canada
slides.text: That is why they are often called living fossils: their body plan has changed little in all that time.

slides.heading: Blue blood that saves lives
slides.text: Their blood carries oxygen with hemocyanin, a copper-based protein that turns dark blue when it holds oxygen. An extract of their blood cells is used in the LAL test, which detects bacterial toxins in medicines. The crabs are returned to the sea after bleeding, but an estimated 10 to 30% of them die.

slides.question: Why is being flipped over dangerous for a horseshoe crab?
slides.explanation: Currents often flip them, and stranded on their backs they are vulnerable to suffocation, so righting themselves matters.
